text: Master data forms the foundation of the application. Most modules cannot function without the corresponding master records being populated first. Master data is managed under Masters (/masters) and Admin (/admin). All master data is tenant-scoped - records created for your hospital are not visible to other hospitals.

The application uses a strict geographic hierarchy: Country > Region > Province/City > Barangay. This cascades through patient registration and any module needing address data. The cascading logic (from PatientCrud Livewire) works as follows:

items: When Country is selected: the regions array is populated from Region::where('country_id', $value)->orderBy('name'). The region_id, province_id, city_id, and barangay_id fields AND their dropdown arrays are ALL reset.

When Region is selected: the provinces array is populated from ProvinceCity::where('region_id', $value)->where('type', 'province')->orderBy('name'). The province_id, city_id, and barangay_id fields AND their arrays are reset.

When Province is selected: the cities array is populated from ProvinceCity::where('parent_id', $value)->where('type', 'city')->orderBy('name'). The city_id and barangay_id fields AND arrays are reset.
When City is selected: the barangays array is populated from Barangay::where('province_city_id', $value)->orderBy('name'). The barangay_id field is reset.

Each level uses a separate database table: countries, regions (with country_id FK), provinces_cities (shared table with 'type' column = 'province' or 'city', with parent_id FK for cities), and barangays (with province_city_id FK).

text: Route: masters.country (permission: admin.masters). Manages the list of countries. The default is the Philippines. Each country has: id, name, code, is_active, tenant_id, created_by, created_date, updated_by, updated_date, history.

Route: masters.region (permission: admin.masters). Manages Philippine regions (NCR, CAR, Region I through XIII, BARMM). Each region belongs to a country. Fields: id, country_id, name, code, is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns.

Route: masters.province (permission: admin.masters). Uses the provinces_cities shared table with type='province'. Each province belongs to a region. Fields: id, region_id, name, code, type (always 'province'), parent_id (null for provinces), is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns.

Route: masters.city (permission: admin.masters). Uses the same provinces_cities table with type='city'. Each city/municipality belongs to a province (parent_id = province_id). Fields: id, region_id, parent_id (points to province), name, code, type (always 'city'), is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns.

Route: masters.barangay (permission: admin.masters). The barangay (village/district) level. Each barangay belongs to a city/municipality (province_city_id FK). Fields: id, province_city_id, name, code, is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns.

items: Masters > Gender - gender options (Male, Female, etc.). Fields: id, name, code, is_active, tenant_id, history. Linked to patients via gender_id FK.
Masters > Civil Status - civil status options (Single, Married, Widowed, Separated, Divorced, etc.). Fields: id, name, code, is_active, tenant_id, history. Linked via civil_status_id FK.
Masters > Religion - religious affiliations. Fields: id, name, code, is_active, tenant_id, history. Linked via religion_id FK.
Masters > Nationality - nationalities. Fields: id, name, code, is_active, tenant_id, history. Linked via nationality_id FK.
Masters > Occupation - occupation types. Fields: id, name, code, is_active, tenant_id, history. Linked via occupation_id FK.
Masters > Blood Type - blood types (A, B, AB, O with Rh +/−). Fields: id, name, code, is_active, tenant_id, history. Linked via blood_type_id FK.

Masters > Relationship - relationship types (Self, Spouse, Parent, Sibling, Child, Friend, etc.) used for emergency contacts. Fields: id, name, code, is_active, tenant_id, history. Linked via emergency_relationship.

text: Route: masters.tenant (permission: admin.tenants). Manages the multi-tenant hospital setup. Each tenant record represents one hospital. The DEMO hospital is tenant_id = 1. Fields include: id, name, code, address, contact, email, phone, is_active, history, audit columns. This is the hospital profile.

Route: masters.department (permission: admin.departments). Clinical departments (Cardiology, General Surgery, Pediatrics, Obstetrics, Emergency, Laboratory, Radiology, Pharmacy, etc.). Departments link to doctors and drive appointment booking. Fields: id, dept_name, dept_code, description, is_active, tenant_id, history. The ER department has dept_code='ER' (looked up by ErAdmissionCrud). Department ID is used in patient registration's primary_care_provider and in appointments.
Route: masters.hospital (permission: admin.masters). Additional hospital/facility records (for multi-facility setups). Fields: id, name, code, address, is_active, tenant_id, history.

Route: masters.users (permission: admin.users). User account CRUD. Fields: id, email, password (hashed), full_name, role (superadmin/tenant_admin/doctor/nurse/etc.), health_care_professional_id (FK to healthcare_professionals for doctor users), department_id, is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns. User role determines which permissions they get. The health_care_professional_id links a doctor user to their HCP record - this is how the system knows which doctor's appointments to show on the schedule.

The permission system is granular and role-based. Every route requires a permission string. The flow: create roles (Admin > Roles) -> assign permissions to roles (Admin > Role Permissions) -> assign roles to users (Masters > Users or Admin > User Permissions).

Route: admin.roles (permission: admin.masters). Create and manage roles. A role is a named collection of permissions (e.g. 'Pharmacist', 'Billing Officer', 'Superadmin'). Fields: id, name, description, is_active, created_by, created_date, history.

Route: admin.role-permissions (permission: admin.masters). Assign granular permissions to each role. This is where you control exactly what each role can do. The interface shows all available permissions grouped by module, with checkboxes to toggle each permission on/off for the selected role.

Route: admin.audit-log (permission: admin.masters). Shows the complete system-wide audit trail. Every create, update, and soft-delete across ALL modules is logged here with: the user who made the change (created_by/updated_by), the timestamp (created_date/updated_date), the model/table affected, the record ID, and the old/new values. This is the compliance and troubleshooting reference.

Route: admin.users.permissions ({userId}, permission: admin.users). Override or fine-tune permissions for an individual user. This lets you give a specific user access to a module that their role doesn't normally grant, or restrict a user below their role's default permissions.

Route: /patients (permission: patient.view, Livewire component: PatientCrud). This is the patient demographic master - the central patient record that all other modules reference. The PatientCrud Livewire handles create, read, update, delete, search, and pagination.
The Patient model has 70+ fields organized into these groups. All fields use snake_case in the code and Livewire components:

items: patient_code - Unique patient identifier. Auto-generated as YYYY + 10-digit zero-padded sequence (e.g. 202600000001). Stored as string, max 20 chars. UNIQUE constraint per tenant: unique:patients,patient_code,NULL,id,tenant_id,{tid},history,1. Can be overridden but must remain unique.
suffix - Nullable, string, max 20 chars (e.g. Jr., Sr., III).
date_of_birth - Nullable, date format. Used to compute age for certificates.
maiden_name - Nullable, string, max 60 chars. (EMR standard field.)
place_of_birth - Nullable, string, max 255 chars. (EMR standard field.)
preferred_language - Nullable, string, max 60 chars. (EMR standard field.)
national_id_no - Nullable, string, max 30 chars (PhilHealth ID, SSS, GSIS, PWD ID, etc.). (EMR standard field.)
passport_no - Nullable, string, max 30 chars. (EMR standard field.)
multiple_birth_indicator - Boolean. Indicates if the patient is part of a multiple birth.
is_deceased - Boolean. Marks the patient as deceased.
date_of_death - Nullable, date. Only relevant if is_deceased is true.
primary_care_provider_id - Nullable, FK to health_care_professionals.id. The patient's primary care physician.
is_philhealth_member - Boolean toggle. When checked, reveals the philhealth_member_id dropdown.
philhealth_member_id - Nullable, FK to philhealth_members.id. Links the patient to a PhilHealth membership record. This must exist BEFORE you can link it. Enables PhilHealth claims.
email - Nullable, email format, max 100 chars.
country_id - Nullable, FK to countries.id. When set, triggers region dropdown load.
region_id - Nullable, FK to regions.id. When set, triggers province dropdown load.
province_id - Nullable, FK to provinces_cities.id (type='province'). When set, triggers city dropdown load.
city_id - Nullable, FK to provinces_cities.id (type='city'). When set, triggers barangay dropdown load.
emergency_relationship - Nullable, string, max 60 chars. Typically from the relationship master.
is_active - Boolean, default true. Set to false to soft-deactivate the patient (they disappear from normal views but remain in DB).
created_by / created_date - Audit trail: who created and when.
updated_by / updated_date - Audit trail: who last modified and when.

text: Step-by-step from the PatientCrud Livewire source code:

items: Navigate to /patients. Click 'Create New Patient' (openCreate method). The form resets, patient_code is auto-generated by generatePatientCode(), isEditing=false, is_philhealth_member=false, showModal=true.

generatePatientCode(): Gets current year (now()->format('Y')), finds the last patient with patient_code LIKE 'YYYY%' for this tenant (withoutGlobalScope('current')), parses the numeric suffix, increments by 1, pads to 10 digits. Returns e.g. '202600000001'.
Fill in patient identifiers: patient_code (auto, can override), last_name (required), first_name (required), middle_name, suffix.

Fill in demographics: date_of_birth, gender_id (dropdown from genders master), civil_status_id, religion_id, nationality_id, occupation_id, blood_type_id, maiden_name, place_of_birth, preferred_language.
Fill in family: father_name, mother_maiden_name, spouse_name, multiple_birth_indicator (checkbox).
Set vital status: is_deceased (checkbox), date_of_death (if deceased), primary_care_provider_id (dropdown from healthcare_professionals).

Set PhilHealth: check is_philhealth_member to reveal the philhealth_member_id dropdown. Select an existing PhilHealth member record. If no member record exists, create one first under PhilHealth > Members.

Fill in address using the cascading dropdowns: select country -> region dropdown populates -> select region -> province dropdown populates -> select province -> city dropdown populates -> select city -> barangay dropdown populates. Then fill address_street and zip_code.
Fill in emergency contact: emergency_contact_name, emergency_contact_no, emergency_relationship.
Set is_active (default true - uncheck only to deactivate).

Click Save. Validation runs (see 4.3). On success: patient is created with created_by = current user ID, created_date = now(), updated_by = current user ID, updated_date = now(), is_active = true, history = 1. Session flash message: 'Patient created successfully.'
After save, the patient appears in the list and can be searched, edited, or viewed on the patient chart.

text: The PatientCrud Livewire has validation rules for every field (the complete rules() method returns these):

items: patient_code: required, string, max:20, UNIQUE per tenant (unique:patients,patient_code,NULL,id,tenant_id,{tid},history,1). On edit, the rule excludes the current record: unique:patients,patient_code,{editingId},id,tenant_id,{tid},history,1.

text: The patient list (mount() method) shows all active patients for the current tenant with pagination (perPage = 10, configurable). Features:

items: Search box: updates on every keystroke (updatingSearch resets page). Filters by patient_code, last_name, first_name, middle_name, contact_no, or philhealth_member_id (PhilHealth number). Uses LIKE '%search%' on each field via a query scope.
Sort: click column headers to sort by patient_code, last_name, first_name, date_of_birth, created_date. Toggle asc/desc. Default sort: patient_code asc.
Row actions: View Chart (opens patient chart), Edit (opens edit modal), Delete (soft-deletes - sets history=0).
The list shows: patient_code, full name (last, first, middle, suffix), gender, age (computed from date_of_birth), PhilHealth status (member or not), contact_no, and address summary.
Patient codes follow the format: 202600000001 (year + 10-digit zero-padded sequence). The year prefix allows yearly resets.

text: Click Edit on a patient row (openEdit method). The system:

items: Loads the patient with all related masters eager-loaded: gender, civilStatus, religion, nationality, occupation, bloodType, country, region, province, city, barangay.
Populates every form field from the loaded record, including null-safe fallbacks (?? '') for all 70+ fields.

Calls loadCascadingForEdit() to populate the cascading dropdown arrays for the patient's current address: regions (where country_id matches), provinces (where region_id matches and type='province'), cities (where parent_id matches and type='city'), barangays (where province_city_id matches).
On save: re-runs validation, then updates ALL fields with updated_by = current user, updated_date = now().
The cascading dropdowns in edit mode work the same as create mode - updating country_id resets region/province/city/barangay fields and their arrays, etc.

text: The View Chart link on each patient row opens the patient chart - a consolidated view of the patient's complete clinical history: all OPD consultations, ER admissions, inpatient admissions, lab requests and results, pharmacy requests and dispensing, CSR requests, radiology requests and results, procedure requests, and billing invoices/payments. The chart is the single source of truth for a patient's clinical record.
